answer: Anchor every agent identity to a harbor of time-decaying reputation: standing rises only from verified useful work (attesting real transactions) and erodes like a tide when idle, so a fake identity cannot wander in, sit still, and keep its privileges. To re-enter the harbor it must redo the work, and each re-entry costs a fresh stake that is slashed if peers catch it attesting fraud. Attackers therefore pay a recurring work-plus-stake cost per identity forever, while honest agents pay once and maintain standing through the work they already do.
